title: Cancelling a base change against a module over the bigger ring
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $M$ an $S$-module (an $R$-module via $R\to S$) and $N$ an $R$-module. Then there is an isomorphism of $S$-modules $c_N:M\otimes_S(S\otimes_RN)\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_RN$, $m\otimes(s\otimes n)\mapsto sm\otimes n$, with inverse $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes(1\otimes n)$. It is natural in $N$: for an $R$-linear map $u:N\to N'$ one has $(1_M\otimes_R u)\circ c_N=c_{N'}\circ(1_M\otimes_S(1_S\otimes_R u))$.
